concept.title: Welcome to uFTi
concept.shortdesc: An app for your family tree that ties every fact to the place you found it.

conbody.p: You add people, families and facts. For each fact, you say where you found it. Later you can see what backs it up.

section.title: What uFTi is
section.p: There is one uFTi app for each kind of device: Windows, Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android. Each app is built for its own device. It is not a web page.
Here is the same family, the Brontë family of Haworth, on a phone and on a Windows computer.

section.title: Where things stand
section.p: uFTi is in Alpha. That is an early stage, so the apps and these pages still change. Alpha-1 is not open to the public yet.
The manuals match Alpha-1. The Windows, Android phone, Android tablet and iPhone manuals are the fullest. The iPad and Mac manuals are shorter.
Everything on these pages is about the uFTi apps.

section.title: Your family tree files
section.p: Family history programs share trees as files in a format called GEDCOM. uFTi uses the newest version, GEDCOM 7, as its own. It also reads and writes the older GEDCOM 5.5.1, so you can move a tree to and from an older program.

section.title: Who makes uFTi
section.p: Oughtibridge Ltd makes uFTi. It is a company in the United Kingdom, set up in 1994. Its particular skill is robust data architecture. That means planning how information is stored so that it stays correct and can be checked.

The company also helps to write international standards. It leads standards projects, and it convenes working groups, in ISO and in IEC. ISO is the International Organization for Standardization. IEC is the International Electrotechnical Commission. Both publish standards. A standard is a set of rules that people agree on, so that things made by different people work together.
We bring the same care to uFTi, where the data are the facts of your family.
